clue.text: First ever set of instructions to be handed down?

definitions.text: First ever set of instructions to be handed down?

parts.note: surface reading: the earliest instruction manual or rule book ever written
setter's reading: rules literally handed down from Mount Sinai on stone tablets, and passed down through generations

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what the very first instruction leaflet ever passed on to people was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handed down' means both passed on through tradition and given down from a mountain, as Moses brought the tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible God gives Moses ten laws on stone tablets, the founding moral code of Judaism and Christianity.

clue.text: Fine pals excited in every minute of existence

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Good friends are thrilled by every single moment they are alive.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole length of time a living thing exists, from birth to death, covers every minute of its life.

clue.text: Language of one place to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: A tongue spoken in a single spot somewhere up north.
explanation.walkthrough: I and PUT, written upwards in the grid, read TUPI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupi is an indigenous South American tongue of Brazil, historically spoken along its coast.

clue.text: What gets church more disturbed — US state pomp

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: something disturbed has been knocked out of place, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what unsettles a church even further in American state pageantry.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the standard abbreviation for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is formal display and ritual, the stuff of a grand ceremony such as a coronation or state occasion.

clue.text: Suiting a solitary person who went mowing with a dog?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: designed for or run by a single individual, like a small business

definitions.text: who went mowing with a dog?
definitions.note: a description of a person standing for the hyphenated phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the figure in the old counting song who went to mow a meadow with his dog

explanation.walkthrough: The children's song 'One Man Went to Mow' runs: 'one man went to mow, went to mow a meadow, one man and his dog'.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man operation or band is run by a single individual, fitting someone working alone.

clue.text: Very short and round, not entirely pleasant — a woman

indicators.note: something short is cut off before its end, so the last letter goes
not the whole thing, so the final letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: the word with its tail cut off
O is round in shape
nice, meaning pleasant, without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a woman who is small, plump and not wholly agreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a female first name, so any woman might be called it; crosswords often clue girls' names this way.

clue.text: It's not plain talk that enthrals any number

definitions.note: a phrase describing something that the adjective applies to

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one word grips the other inside it

parts.note: to orate is to talk in a formal speech
N is the mathematical symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Flowery speech that captivates crowds is anything but plain.
explanation.walkthrough: ORATE holds N after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is the opposite of something simple or unadorned.

clue.text: American author conjuring up new nightmare, yes?

indicators.note: a conjuror makes things appear by magic, so the letters are magicked into a new shape

parts.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A US writer dreaming up a fresh horror story, and the question is whether that's right.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway was the Nobel-winning US novelist who wrote The Old Man and the Sea and A Farewell to Arms.

clue.text: Ruin peace, being terrible person living for good food and drink?

definitions.text: person living for good food and drink

indicators.note: something terrible is a mess, so the letters are scrambled out of order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dreadful guest who spoils the calm, all for the love of fine dining.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure, after the philosopher Epicurus, is someone devoted to refined pleasures, especially eating and wine.

clue.text: Mistake made by Eastern bishop getting nothing right

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
O looks like zero
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An Orthodox bishop slips up by coming away with nothing correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The Right Reverend is the formal style of an Anglican bishop, shortened to RR.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a blunder or slip, the plain synonym for something done wrong.

clue.text: Garment with classic hem is exquisite

indicators.note: with here means held within, so the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: runs from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing with a timeless, beautiful hemline.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemise is a loose shift or slip, a simple dress or undergarment.

clue.text: Where boat stops, beastly noise is coming with anger

parts.note: the sound a cow makes
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: At a jetty, an awful racket arrives along with someone's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A moorage is a place for mooring vessels, where a craft is tied up and comes to rest.

clue.text: Maureen facing gym gets to be depressed

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen
PE is physical education, the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: Maureen, confronted by a gym session, ends up feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to sulk listlessly, wandering around in a gloomy, dejected mood.

clue.text: In agreement with firm having an event

parts.note: Co is short for company
an incident is an occurrence or event

explanation.surface: Agreeing with a company that is holding a function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective but is a noun, a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincident means corresponding exactly or concurring, so things coincident are in harmony with each other.

clue.text: Man's yet to be freed, getting pardon

indicators.note: letters set free from their order can be rearranged however they like

parts.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A prisoner awaiting release finally receives a reprieve.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon, typically granted to many offenders at once by a government.

clue.text: Long-distance travellers in camp seen relaxing

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things, so the letters slacken out of their fixed order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Hikers on a long trek are spotted resting at their campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-distance travellers' suggests hikers or lorry drivers; the journey is to the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts journey vast distances beyond Earth, the furthest any human traveller goes.

clue.text: Wrap up little son needing sort of walk

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, and little hints at shortening
a duck-like rocking gait

explanation.surface: Bundle up a toddler who needs to get walking.
explanation.definitionFit: To swaddle is to wrap a baby snugly in cloth, binding it up tightly.

clue.text: Charlatan showed sign of injury and shuffled along

parts.note: a sham is an impostor or fraud
bleeding is a sign of a wound

explanation.surface: A fraudster faked a wound and limped off.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk awkwardly, dragging the feet, much the same as shuffling.

clue.text: Their logs are not for burning

definitions.text: Their logs are not for burning

parts.note: surface reading: wood stacked by some householders that will never go on the fire
setter's reading: a log is also a written daily record, which its keepers want preserved

explanation.surface: Some people keep a pile of timber that they refuse to put on the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: People who keep journals record each day's events, and such a record is called a log.

clue.text: Economist's work I'd ask a pal about — time to get stuck into it

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other
about can mean turned around or scattered, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone plans to consult a friend about an economics text before knuckling down to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters rearrange to DASKAPIAL, and T goes in before the final AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx, the economist and philosopher, wrote Das Kapital, his critique of capitalism.

clue.text: Supper's beginning with fruit and broccoli?

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
pears are a common fruit

explanation.surface: A dinner that starts with fruit followed by greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: broccoli is sold as spears.
explanation.definitionFit: Long stems of sprouting broccoli or asparagus are called spears, so broccoli can come as these.

clue.text: International performance not broken up

parts.note: Int is a short form of international
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A global show that did not split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means whole and undamaged, with nothing missing or shattered.

clue.text: Normal industry not entirely evident in African country

indicators.note: only part of the next words shows, so the letters are found partly visible inside them

parts.note: runs across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Ordinary manufacturing barely shows up in an African nation's economy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African state whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: First woman to pause where there's a stiff climb

parts.note: in the Bible, Eve was the first woman
to rest is to pause

explanation.surface: The first woman stops for a breather on a steep ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain in the Himalayas, so reaching its summit is an arduous ascent.

clue.text: Sound of dogs in East London location

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the noise dogs make when they bark
second meaning: a district in the borough of ... and Dagenham, in east London

explanation.definitionFit: Barking is both the gerund of what dogs do and the name of a town in outer east London.

clue.text: Like a twisted cord that's not very good

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stringy, resembling a rope
second meaning: British slang for poor quality or slightly unwell

explanation.walkthrough: In British English ropy or ropey is informal for shoddy, as in a ropy old car.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means rope-like and stringy, and colloquially also means inferior or below par.

clue.text: Cake served during breakfast or tea

indicators.note: something served during a meal appears within it, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A cake offered at either the morning meal or afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of central European origin, often made with ground nuts.

clue.text: Lo, a carpet laid out for a queen!

indicators.note: laid out means arranged afresh, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Behold, a rug is unrolled to welcome a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Cleopatra was smuggled to Julius Caesar rolled up in a carpet, so the surface fits her.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling monarch of Ptolemaic Egypt, a famous female sovereign.
